title: 第22章 返程的车队第23章 新的打算
content_zh:
第二天一早，车队就出发了。
安静的大道上没什么新奇事物，除了微风和远处的光景，再无任何事物与旅人作伴。
柯林捂着发疼的脑袋坐在马车副座上。
坐在马车后边的凯斯倒是精神百倍，好像昨天什么都没发生似的。
可能酒水真的对兽人有什么不为人知的神秘效果？柯林不禁开始怀疑。
“柯林老兄，你昨天喝得太狠了。”
鲍勃笑着拍了拍对方的肩膀，然后递出水袋：“这是我今早找人泡的茶，可能对你有好处。”
接过来喝了口，柯林只感觉舌头都被苦没知觉了。
不过好在头疼的感觉确实减轻了许多，难怪上了年纪的鲍勃现在状态看着还不错。
鲍勃笑道：“还行吧？”
“倒是挺提神的。”柯林拍了拍后脑勺说：“这趟咱们得小心着点，我听村长说一头巨熊正在周围肆虐呢。”
“一头熊可比一群狼好对付多了。”凯斯说：“车队里这么多人呢，把它搞死了每人至少都能拿上几个金币。”
听到这话，周围马车上的冒险者朝着凯斯欢呼起来。
相比去时的暗自嫌弃，冒险者们和这半兽人的关系倒是好了不少。
“到时候还得靠你们呢，老兄。”鲍勃说。
柯林默默说：“也许吧。”
不过这次，车队一直走出去很远都没遇上什么麻烦。
秋日的阳光不算特别晒人，海面吹来的微风清爽宜人。
坐在马车上摇摇晃晃的柯林感觉前所未有的轻松。
价值十几个金币的皮甲外加满满当当的草药袋。

就单纯只算草药的话，卖出去后他和凯斯少说都能分到九个金币呢。
九个金币啊！
无论怎么算，这在贫民窟都能算是一笔巨款了！
算出这个数字后。
柯林知道，他这辈子可能都不会和原身一样去当什么码头苦力了。
中间的落差实在太大，反正他是肯定接受不了的。
柯林悠闲地靠在马车上。
穿越过来之后第一次有种放松的感觉。
沉甸甸的钱包将焦虑的心脏压得实实在在的，九个金币足够生活好几个月了，接下来很长一段时间应该都不会像前几天那样着急了。
除此之外，就是两人搞到的两套护甲了。
柯林记得先前在二手市场看过，一件二手棉甲三金币，二手的皮甲好像是九金币来着。
这也能算是这趟的重磅收入了。
对他们这些冒险者来说，武器和护甲基本就等于生产工具了。
不同的是，其他职业的生产工具差，可能只会减少收入，他们的装备差劲，可能就会丢命了。
不过老实说，柯林对使用甲胄还是一知半解的状态。
毕竟前世也不可能有这种经验，关于护甲之类的东西也只是在电影里见过。
或者说应该花钱找个退休佣兵之类的人物学学？
柯林记得在贫民窟里这样的课程一节就要几个银币来着，而且老实说，他也觉得那些教授课程的老佣兵其实也不怎么可靠。
但是要去城内找卫兵队长之类的人学习的话，花的钱又实在太多。
当然，这也是必要的开销。

在这个世界上，甲胄的使用方法其实有很多流派。
就像是握剑乱挥和学会某个流派的剑术不是一回事儿那样，单纯的把甲胄往身上一套和学会一种着甲战斗方式同样不能划等号。
后者肯定是需要花钱的。
content_en:
Early the next morning, the convoy set off.
There is nothing new on the quiet road. Apart from the breeze and the scenery in the distance, there is nothing to accompany the traveler.
Colin held his aching head and sat on the passenger seat of the carriage.
Case, who was sitting behind the carriage, was in great spirits, as if nothing happened yesterday.
Maybe alcohol really has some unknown and mysterious effect on orcs? Colin couldn't help but start to doubt.
"Brother Colin, you drank too much yesterday."
Bob smiled and patted the other person's shoulder, then handed over the water bag: "This is the tea I asked someone to make this morning. It may be good for you."
Taking it and taking a sip, Colin felt that his tongue was numb from the pain.
But fortunately, the headache has indeed eased a lot. No wonder the elderly Bob seems to be in good condition now.
Bob smiled and said, "Is it okay?"
"It's quite refreshing." Colin patted the back of his head and said, "We have to be careful this time. I heard from the village chief that a giant bear is raging around."
"A bear is much easier to deal with than a pack of wolves." Case said, "There are so many people in the convoy. If we kill it, everyone can get at least a few gold coins."
Hearing this, the adventurers on the surrounding carriages cheered towards Case.
Compared to the secret dislike they felt when they left, the relationship between the adventurers and this half-orc is much better.
"It's going to be up to you then, man," Bob said.
Colin said silently: "Maybe."
But this time, the team went all the way without any trouble.
The autumn sunshine is not particularly dazzling, and the breeze blowing from the sea is refreshing and pleasant.
Colin, who was swaying in the carriage, felt more relaxed than ever.
Leather armor worth more than a dozen gold coins and a bag full of herbal medicine.
Just counting the herbs, he and Case would both get nine gold coins after selling them.
Nine gold coins!
No matter how you calculate it, this is a huge sum of money in the slums!
After calculating this number.
Colin knew that he might never be a dock coolie like his original self.
The gap in the middle is really too big, and he definitely can't accept it anyway.
Colin leaned leisurely on the carriage.
For the first time since traveling through time, I felt relaxed.
The heavy wallet weighed heavily on my anxious heart. Nine gold coins were enough to live on for several months. I probably wouldn't be as anxious as I was a few days ago for a long time to come.
Apart from that, there are two sets of armors that the two of them obtained.
Colin remembered that he had seen it in the second-hand market before. A second-hand cotton armor cost three gold coins, and a second-hand leather armor seemed to cost nine gold coins.
This can also be regarded as the heavy income of this trip.
For adventurers like them, weapons and armor are basically production tools.
The difference is that if other professions have poor production tools, their income may only be reduced, while if their equipment is poor, they may lose their lives.
But to be honest, Colin still has little understanding of how to use armor.
After all, it was impossible to have this kind of experience in the previous life, and I had only seen things like armor in movies.
Or should I spend money to find someone like a retired mercenary to learn from me?
Colin remembered that such a course in the slums cost several silver coins, and to be honest, he also felt that the old mercenaries who taught the courses were not very reliable.
But if you go to the city to learn from someone like the guard captain, it will cost too much.
Of course, this is also a necessary expense.
In this world, there are actually many schools of thought in how to use armor.
Just as holding a sword and swinging it wildly is not the same thing as learning a certain style of swordsmanship, simply putting a set of armor on one's body is not the same thing as learning a way to fight wearing armor.
The latter definitely costs money.
